# PCI Authorization Guide

## CPT Codes — Elective PCI

| CPT | Description | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 92920 | Percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA); single major coronary artery or branch | Balloon angioplasty — single vessel |
| 92921 | PTCA; each additional branch of a major coronary artery | Additional vessel — add-on code |
| 92928 | Percutaneous transcatheter placement of intracoronary stent(s), with coronary angioplasty when performed; single major coronary artery or branch | PCI with stent — single vessel (most common) |
| 92929 | PCI with stent; each additional branch of a major coronary artery | Additional stent — add-on code |
| 92933 | PCI with atherectomy (rotational, orbital, laser) and stent; single major coronary artery or branch | Complex PCI with atherectomy |
| 92934 | PCI with atherectomy and stent; each additional branch | Atherectomy — add-on code |
| 92941 | PCI for acute MI; single major coronary artery or branch | Primary PCI for STEMI — NOT for elective PCI |
| 92943 | PCI for chronic total occlusion; single major coronary artery or branch | CTO-PCI — requires specific documentation |
| 93454 | Catheter placement in coronary artery(s) for coronary angiography, including intraprocedural injection(s) for coronary angiography | Diagnostic coronary angiography |
| 93571 | Intravascular Doppler velocity and/or pressure derived coronary flow reserve measurement (FFR) | FFR/iFR measurement — supports medical necessity |

## ICD-10 Codes

| ICD-10 | Description | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I25.10 | Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris | Stable CAD — requires objective ischemia evidence |
| I25.110 | Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery with unstable angina pectoris | Unstable angina — higher urgency |
| I25.119 | Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery with unspecified angina pectoris | Angina — specify CCS class in documentation |
| I25.5 | Ischemic cardiomyopathy | Reduced LVEF from CAD |
| I25.700 | Atherosclerosis of coronary artery bypass graft(s), unspecified, without angina pectoris | SVG or arterial graft disease |
| I20.0 | Unstable angina | ACS spectrum — may not require elective PA |
| I25.2 | Old myocardial infarction | Prior MI with residual ischemia |
| I25.84 | Coronary artery disease in patient with history of repaired congenital heart disease | Complex anatomy |

## Payer Requirements

Payer tabs: Medicare, Medicaid, Private.

### Medicare

**Required Documentation**
- Objective evidence of myocardial ischemia (stress test, FFR ≤0.80, iFR ≤0.89, or nuclear imaging)
- Coronary anatomy documented by diagnostic catheterization
- Symptoms (angina CCS Class ≥II) or high-risk stress test findings despite optimal medical therapy
- SYNTAX score documentation for multi-vessel or left main disease
- Heart Team discussion documentation for 3-vessel or left main disease
- Informed consent documenting discussion of PCI vs CABG vs OMT
- Operator and facility volume requirements met (≥75 PCIs/year operator, ≥200/year facility)

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- Significant coronary stenosis (≥70% by angiography or ≥50% left main) with objective ischemia
- Symptoms refractory to optimal medical therapy
- High-risk stress test findings (≥10% ischemic territory, LVEF <35%, hypotension)
- FFR ≤0.80 confirming hemodynamic significance

**Reimbursement Note:** Medicare covers elective PCI under NCD 20.7. Requires documentation of objective ischemia. ISCHEMIA trial data supports OMT-first approach for stable CAD — document why revascularization is preferred over continued OMT.

**Known Payer Policies**
- [Covered] Medicare (CMS): Covered per NCD 20.7; objective ischemia required; SYNTAX score required for multi-vessel/LM disease
- [Covered] Medicare Advantage (varies): Generally follows CMS NCD; some plans require additional documentation

### Medicaid

**Required Documentation**
- State-specific prior authorization required
- Objective ischemia documentation
- Coronary anatomy by diagnostic catheterization
- Cardiology consultation note
- Failure of or contraindication to optimal medical therapy

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- Significant coronary stenosis with objective ischemia
- Symptomatic despite medical therapy
- High-risk anatomy (left main, proximal LAD, 3-vessel disease with reduced LVEF)

**Reimbursement Note:** Medicaid coverage varies by state. Most states require prior authorization for elective PCI. Some states limit coverage to specific indications. Contact state Medicaid office for current policy.

**Known Payer Policies**
- [Covered] Medicaid (state-specific): Coverage varies; prior authorization typically required; follow state-specific LCD criteria

### Private

**Required Documentation**
- Prior authorization required by virtually all commercial payers
- Objective evidence of ischemia (stress test, FFR, nuclear imaging, stress echo)
- Diagnostic coronary angiography report with stenosis measurements
- Documentation of optimal medical therapy trial (typically ≥3 months) unless contraindicated
- SYNTAX score for multi-vessel or left main disease
- Heart Team note for complex anatomy
- Cardiology/interventional cardiology consultation note
- Peer-to-peer review available if denied

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- Coronary stenosis ≥70% (≥50% left main) with objective ischemia
- Angina CCS Class ≥II or anginal equivalent despite OMT
- High-risk stress test (large ischemia, LVEF drop, hypotension, ST changes in ≥5 leads)
- FFR ≤0.80 or iFR ≤0.89 confirming hemodynamic significance
- SYNTAX score ≤22 for multi-vessel disease (PCI preferred over CABG)

**Reimbursement Note:** Commercial payers frequently deny elective PCI without documented OMT trial. ISCHEMIA trial (2020) showed no mortality benefit of PCI over OMT for stable CAD — document symptom burden and quality-of-life impact. FFR documentation significantly reduces denial rates.

**Known Payer Policies**
- [Covered] UnitedHealthcare: Requires objective ischemia; FFR documentation reduces denials; SYNTAX score required for LM/3VD
- [Covered] Aetna: Covers elective PCI with documented ischemia and failed OMT; peer-to-peer available
- [Covered] Cigna: Requires OMT documentation; FFR/iFR strongly recommended for intermediate lesions
- [Covered] Anthem/BCBS: Prior auth required; SYNTAX score and Heart Team note for complex anatomy
- [Covered] Humana: Covers per ACC/AHA appropriateness criteria; may require OMT documentation
